Getting started: your first session

Everything you need for the first twenty minutes: starting a world, moving around, finding your pack and leaving without losing anything.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 7 min read · New players · feature ledger · all guides
Contents

  2. The start menu

Before you start

Play with keyboard and mouse. Keys here are defaults; change gameplay assignments in Settings > Controls > Key bindings. Keys follow physical positions, so on another keyboard layout use the QWERTY positions or assign keys that suit you. Keyboard, mouse and controller support

The window opens at 1280 × 720 and cannot be made smaller than 800 × 450. Press F11 or Alt + Enter to toggle borderless fullscreen; the game does not remember fullscreen between launches. Window, fullscreen and title

Tip. For installation, updating and finding worlds, see Install, update and find your worlds. This page starts at the game’s menu.

The start menu

Choose Continue to resume the loaded world or Worlds to choose or create one. Continue is unavailable when no usable world is loaded. Multiplayer, Structure workshop, Settings, Credits and Quit are also on the menu. Start menu

Key or actionWhat it does
Arrow keysMove the selection.
Enter or clickOpen the selected entry.
EscReturn from a sub-page.
  • Continue resumes the loaded world.
  • Worlds lists saves and opens the creation dialog.
  • Settings opens graphics, audio, control and interface preferences.
  • Credits has seven cards. Use Left/Right or Previous/Next to browse; Tab selects a footer button, and Enter or Space activates it. Esc or Skip credits returns to the menu. Credits
Tip. These steps cover the base game.

Create your first world

  1. Choose Worlds, then Create world.
  2. Enter a name. Leave Seed blank for a fresh seed or enter unsigned decimal digits to reuse a seed.
  3. Choose Creative or Survival. Leave terrain generation at the current default unless you need an older one.
  4. Choose Create world or press Enter. Esc or Cancel returns without creating a world.

A new world's pack contains 12 Berries, 2 Water flasks, 1 Empty flask and 4 Alder board pieces. Switching modes and respawning do not grant another starter pack. New worlds: creative by default, survival starter supplies

Tip. Select a world in the list, then choose Play world, press Enter or double-click its row. One click only selects it. For rename, duplicate, backup and recovery steps, see Install, update and find your worlds. Worlds: create, play, rename, duplicate and back up
Tip. Star worlds you want to find quickly, then use the Starred filter. Worlds: create, play, rename, duplicate and back up
Careful. To delete a world, select it and hold Delete world (or the Delete key) for 3 seconds; letting go early cancels. Deleting removes the save for good and cannot be undone, so make a backup first with Create backup. The world you are currently in cannot be deleted. Worlds: create, play, rename, duplicate and back up

Look and move

Click the world once to capture the mouse. That first click never mines or places a block. While the mouse is released (after opening a panel, pressing Esc, or switching away from the window) you cannot move or look. Closing a panel captures the mouse again on its own. Mouse capture and release

Key or actionWhat it does
W / A / S / DWalk forward, left, back, right (about 4.3 m/s). You step up half-metre blocks without jumping.
MouseLook around.
SpaceJump about 1.25 m; hold it to jump again on every landing. A full one-metre block needs a jump.
Shift (hold)Sneak at about 1.3 m/s; you cannot walk off an edge while sneaking.
Ctrl + W (hold)Sprint at about 5.6 m/s.
CCrawl through gaps 0.6 m tall; press C or Space again to stand.
F or double-tap SpaceStart or stop flying (creative only). Space rises, Shift descends, Ctrl boosts.

Leaves and needles do not block you. Walk into a tree crown at half speed, hold Space to climb up and Shift to climb down, or let go to stay where you are. You can stand on top of a crown; hold Shift as you land to sink into it. Moving and climbing through leaves

Walking speeds do not depend on frame rate, because movement runs on a fixed 60 Hz step. Walking and looking around

Tip. The default F10 key saves a game screenshot and reports the saved path. Print Screen releases the pointer for your system screenshot tool. Clean view (F1)

Read the screen

  • Top left: the status line. Actions report here, for example 'Collected … ×3' or 'Capacity full; block left behind'.
  • Top right, left of the map: the looking-at card, shown when you aim at a block within 6 m. F2 hides or shows it, the same as Settings > Interface > Layout > Target info.
  • Top right: the compact map, with the FPS and coordinates box beneath it. The box is on by default; turn it off in Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics.
  • Lower right: the collection feed. It shows what you gained, for example '+3 Oak wood', for a few seconds. Crafting, creative mining and home storage do not show there.
  • Middle: the crosshair, and a small action hint under it.
  • Lower left (survival only): the four bars for health, hunger, thirst and stamina.
  • Bottom: the ten-slot hotbar and the label of the selected item.

Press the default F1 key to hide the HUD, crosshair and hands, then F10 to save a screenshot. Press F1 again to restore the view. The pause menu also has Screenshot. Clean view (F1)

Open your pack and the hotbar

Press E to open or close the inventory. Switch tabs with the mouse, Tab or Shift+Tab. Creative has the free Build catalog; Survival carpentry adds Build when you carry a Furniture hammer. The pack holds up to 1000 capacity. The header at the top right shows your load, for example "Load: 0.1 / 1000". Inventory screen and its tabs Carry capacity (mass-based pack)

Pack shows carried items as a paged icon grid. Hover for the name, quantity and help; click to use or equip an item. Ctrl+F searches by name, and the sort button switches between grouped and alphabetical order. Dragging inside Pack does not rearrange or split your stock. Pack tab: Items and Character Compact inventory grid

The hotbar

The hotbar has ten slots that start empty. A slot is a shortcut to an item kind, not a container, so its number is everything of that kind in your pack.

Key or actionWhat it does
1 – 9, 0Select slot 1 to 10.
Mouse wheel, [ and ]Cycle through the slots.
Hover an item + 1 – 9 or 0Bind that item to the slot (inventory open).
Drag an item onto a slotBind it. Dragging a slot onto another swaps them; dragging a slot off the bar clears it.

With the inventory closed, Tab cycles through the tools and weapons you carry and back to empty hands. Your hotbar slot assignments are saved with the world. Ten-slot hotbar

Tip. In survival, J drops one selected carried item; Ctrl+J drops everything of that kind. With Pack open, hover its icon first. Approach a dropped stack after a short delay to collect what fits. Items on the ground and manual dropping

Creative and survival

There are exactly two modes. Press F4 to switch, except on the start menu, while joined to someone else's server, or while a stopped host waits for recovery. When you host a world, the switch happens once the server confirms it. Your pack, hotbar and position stay as they are, and each world remembers the mode you left it in. Creative and survival modes (F4)

Creative

  • Blocks break instantly and placing is free; crafting is free.
  • The Build tab and catalog, middle-click block picking, building brushes and undo.
  • Flight, map travel and teleport.
  • Editable time, weather and season.

Survival

  • Blocks take time to mine and your pack is limited to 1000 capacity.
  • Four bars for health, hunger, thirst and stamina, shown lower left.
  • Falls hurt, and you eat with R, drink with T and quick-craft with X.
  • Dying opens a screen showing the cause and respawn location. Press Enter or click Respawn when ready; you keep your inventory. Death and respawn

Items you took from the creative catalog stay in your pack after you switch to survival. Continue with Your first survival day.

Pause, save and quit

Press Esc for the pause menu, then choose Settings. Esc first closes an active panel or dialog. From in-game Settings, Back or Esc returns to the pause menu; Resume returns to play. Local play pauses; a connected server continues. Settings menu basics Esc key and what pauses the game

Key or actionWhat it does
EscClose the active panel or open the pause menu.
F6Save your local world, or the world you host, now ('World saved safely'). In a server world you joined, nothing is written on your computer and the game says 'This session does not save the world locally'.
Save & main menuSave and return to the start menu (pause menu).
Ctrl + Q, Save & quit or the window's close buttonSave, then quit. If saving fails, the game stays open.

For autosaves, backups and recovery, see Saves and world files. Graphics, sound, interface settings and key bindings follow you between worlds; world time, weather and season remain local. Saving, Main menu and quitting
